name: document
description: Full-page document container with repeatable print headers, footers, and page counters

changes.note: Print moves onto named pages. The pattern's @page rules were unnamed, so once bundled every printed page of an app took the document's margins and its 'Page N / M' counter; a document now prints on @page faqir-document (paper and margins from the --page-* tokens, as before) and a page without a document prints on the browser's defaults. A document that states both data-format and data-orientation pins its paper with a literal named page (faqir-document-a4-portrait, …-letter-landscape), so one file can print A4 and Letter documents. A change of named page is a forced break — Chromium printed a blank first page when even an empty element preceded a document — so the <body> of a file that prints a document takes the document's page as well; only documents that ask for different paper break between them. New, all opt-in: the counter is localised from the document's lang (de, es, fr, it, nl, pt, ro built in; --doc-page-label / --doc-page-separator / --doc-page-suffix for others); data-running="margin" prints the running header and footer from the --doc-running-header / --doc-running-footer strings in the page-margin boxes, with the footer and counter on one line under one rule; data-header="from-page-2" leaves the running header off the first page; the letter variant is a DIN 5008 business letter (A4, fold marks at 105/210mm, punch mark at 148.5mm, an address slot in the Form B window, data-form="a" for Form A). The report variant reads --doc-serif instead of naming Georgia, and a quote inside a document takes the document's body and legal sizes. Four table tokens give a print theme's table its own voice (forecraft #48): --doc-rule-scale weighs the row rules and --doc-rule-strong-scale the rule under the head (not in a bordered table) and over the totals, as multiples of the theme's edge roles; --doc-table-num-scale sizes number, currency and percent cells; --doc-table-flush takes a row's first and last cell inset away. Every default draws what the table drew before.

The responsive ladder moves onto the breakpoint canon, mobile-first (task 0.8-09). The sheet's max-width media blocks became min-width floors on canon tiers (sm 40rem/640px, md 48rem/768px, lg 64rem/1024px), so every unconditional rule is now the PHONE case and a tier block only ever widens it. The sheet fills a phone edge to edge and gets its margin, padding and rounded corners back at md — the same 768px floor as before. The tier block is declared BEFORE @media print, because a min-width query is true on paper (a Letter page box is 8.5in ≈ 816px) and print must still win. The floors keep their values, so the only behavioural shift is at exactly a floor: 1024px now gets the wide layout rather than the narrow one.

Added canonical doc-header and doc-footer parts, fixed-position browser fallbacks, running-element margin boxes, page counters, and a three-page print reference; legacy header/footer parts remain styled as aliases.

doc-header.description: Canonical running document header; repeats on every printed page

address.description: letter variant only: the recipient's address, between the letterhead (doc-header) and the body. Printed in the DIN 5008 envelope window (--doc-window-top/-left/-width/-height/-padding).

doc-footer.description: Canonical running document footer; repeats on every printed page

header.description: Legacy alias for doc-header; supported for non-breaking upgrades

footer.description: Legacy alias for doc-footer; supported for non-breaking upgrades

theme.description: Theme name applied via data-theme attribute

--doc-running-header.description: The running header as a CSS string, drawn in the top-left page-margin box (custom property). Set it on :root (or <html style>): a page box inherits from the root only, so a value on the article is not seen. Pair with data-running="margin" or data-header="from-page-2" to keep the DOM doc-header for the screen only.

--doc-running-footer.description: The running footer as a CSS string, drawn in the bottom-left page-margin box beside the counter (custom property, set on :root). \A breaks a line. Pair with data-running="margin".

--doc-page-label.description: Text before the page number (custom property, set on :root). The pattern restates it for de, es, fr, it, nl, pt and ro from the document's lang.

--doc-page-separator.description: Text between the page number and the page count (custom property, set on :root).

--doc-page-suffix.description: Text after the page count (custom property, set on :root).

--doc-accent.description: The one accent a print theme inks in; every print theme points --color-primary at it (custom property, set on :root).

chromium.mechanism: position: fixed repetition for full DOM header/footer plus @page margin-box page counters; with data-running="margin" / data-header="from-page-2", margin-box strings from --doc-running-header / --doc-running-footer
chromium.notes: Chrome 131+ supports page-margin generated content and page counters; unsupported running()/element() declarations fall back to fixed positioning. Disable browser-supplied print headers and footers. Named pages (Chrome 85+) give each document its paper; page selector lists are not parsed, so each named page is its own rule. A fixed DOM header repeats on every page, page 1 included — to leave it off page 1, print it as a margin-box string with data-header="from-page-2". Margin boxes inherit only from the root element, so their strings, counter labels and fonts are root custom properties; the pattern reaches them from a document's attributes and lang through :root:has().

prince.mechanism: position: running() with content: element() in @page margin boxes
prince.notes: Native running elements preserve the authored header/footer markup; page and pages counters render in the bottom-right margin box.

weasyprint.mechanism: position: running() with content: element() in @page margin boxes
weasyprint.notes: Native running elements, page-margin boxes, and page counters are supported; the optional element() start parameter is not used.

required_attrs: aria-label describing the document type and title
